thread.text: there is a detailed discussion on the acceptance, effective area, but then it seems that we go on a limb and talk aout the sky coverage, and bring up a comparison with egret that doesn't seem to make much sense

I think we need to disentangle the 3 concepts. the acceptance is related to how many photons we actually "accept", if I understnad correctly, and this is quantified with an area (for some reason), in astrohpysicis.
Another thing is the fraction of the sky being surveyed.

I think the two are connected by the statement that fermi-lat can survey the whole sky in abotut 3h. I guess that, given the acceptance are, and the speed at which it moves/oscilaltes, that's the time it takes to observe the whole sky
I think this is how we should link the two concepts, ask notebooklm for more context on this, and let's reframe this part, simplifying and condensing it a little bit to make it easier to understand.
the comparison with egret seems like something that was added as an afterthought, and it's not really consequential wrt what we said before

[AGENT] Rewrote the effective area/acceptance/sky coverage paragraph. Disentangled the three concepts into a clear causal chain: (1) effective area = per-direction sensitivity, (2) acceptance = effective area integrated over all directions (total photon-collecting power), linked to the 2.4 sr FoV, (3) survey mode leverages the large acceptance for full-sky coverage every 3h. Dropped the EGRET comparison (already covered in Section 2.3.1 lines 46-50). Added cross-reference to Section 2.3.1 for the survey mode details.
